Lectures, Films, Readings, Panels.post_content: No prior dance or house/ball experience required! Benji Hart (they/them), a vogue instructor, Black queer performance artist, writer, and abolitionist educator, will lead a movement-based workshop for the Williams College community. Participants will move their bodies and learn the basics of vogue femme, a dance form that emerged from Black and Latin ballroom communities and has since traveled worldwide. Join the students of WGSS 364 on Wednesday, December 2, from 7:00 to 8:30 p.m. in the Dance Studio at the ’62 Center for Theatre and Dance. Immediately following the workshop, a reception will offer an opportunity for further conversation with Hart about their artistic practice, ballroom history, abolitionist work, and experiences building a career across art, organizing, and political education. More information about Hart's work is available at benjihart.com. Sponsored by: Women's, Gender, and Sexuality Studies; ’62 Center for Theatre and Dance; Office of Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion; Africana Studies; American Studies; and Latina/o Studies. Please RSVP by Saturday, November 28! All are welcome: https://forms.gle/78e5PmdUo2aREtky6

Academic\/&#8203;Teaching\/&#8203;Resear.post_content: Lines in the Sand between Theory and Experiment by Prof. Alec Payne, Williams College, Friday November 20, 1:00 - 1:50pm, North Science Building 015, Wachenheim, Mathematics Colloquium Abstract: What happens when you vibrate a metal plate covered with sand? The sand gathers along beautiful curves called Chladni figures, which represent the zero set of a standing wave on the plate. In this seminar, we'll recreate this experiment and explore the mathematics behind these patterns. We'll then discuss my recent work with Prof. Zihui Zhao (Johns Hopkins University) and what our results tell us about Chladni figures.

Lines in the Sand between Theory and Experiment by Prof. Alec Payne, Williams College, Friday November 20, 1:00 – 1:50pm, North Science Building 015, Wachenheim, Mathematics Colloquium

Abstract: What happens when you vibrate a metal plate covered with sand? The sand gathers along beautiful curves called Chladni figures, which represent the zero set of a standing wave on the plate. In this seminar, we’ll recreate this experiment and explore the mathematics behind these patterns. We’ll then discuss my recent work with Prof. Zihui Zhao (Johns Hopkins University) and what our results tell us about Chladni figures.

Arts at Williams.post_content:
The Williams Gospel Choir offers an afternoon of inspiring song titled Praise In All Seasons. The performance is free and open to all in Chapin Hall.

For over forty years people of all faiths have been invited to join the Gospel Choir to celebrate the tradition and move ahead into a future of joyous song.

The Williams Gospel Choir continues to be a force that uplifts and empowers students and community members alike with their powerful and soulful voices. Its members also continue to consider the historic significance of gospel and the special role it continues to play in the lives of people from all over the world.
